nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Circular economy practices|Extended producer responsibility_qna_000
nodes.label: Taxonomy
nodes.question: What concepts have been established to promote sustainable production in the textile sector?
nodes.answer: Concepts like Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) by the OECD have been established to promote sustainable production in the textile sector.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Circular economy practices|Extended producer responsibility_qna_001
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How do the findings on the effectiveness of Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) initiatives align with Rubio et al. (2019)?
nodes.answer: Both studies highlight the potential of EPR programs in reducing post-consumer waste.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Circular economy practices|Extended producer responsibility_qna_002
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: How could EPR be more effective in addressing waste issues according to the text?
nodes.answer: EPR could be more effective by combining with interventions at the design phase, such as the development of eco-design requirements policies, to target waste reduction from the outset of the product life cycle.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Circular economy practices|Extended producer responsibility_qna_004
nodes.label: Ethics and Regulation
nodes.question: What is Extended Producer Responsibility according to the OECD (2001)?
nodes.answer: According to the OECD (2001), Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) is a policy approach where producers are given a significant responsibility for the treatment or disposal of post-consumer products.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Circular economy practices|Extended producer responsibility_qna_005
nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: How is the European Union addressing waste in the fashion industry?
nodes.answer: The European Union has published new regulations based on the "polluter pays principle" to accelerate circularity in the fashion industry, placing extended producer responsibility (EPR) policy at the centre of these efforts.
